description:
An envelope addressed to a `(to, handle)` queue. Queues are the substrate primitive: one shape carries every envelope, with `to == owner_did` and `handle` a bare slug identifying the queue on the owner's machine. Routing happens at the daemon's endpoint-resolution chain (org-membership lookup), not at parse time. Stamps are allowed on any envelope regardless of recipient — including self-attestations of one's own captures. In MVP the cryptographic stamp covers only the body, not the envelope.

**Bare-slug address shape (substrate-for-themia collapse, 2026-05-21).** `to` is the *queue owner's* DID (the principal whose relay sequences the queue). `handle` is a bare slug — no namespace prefix, no recognized vocabulary of top-level tokens. The pair `(to, handle)` is the canonical wire address; the composite URI form `<to>#<handle>` (e.g. `did:web:themia.pro#assemblee_generale`) is **display-only** and never appears on the wire. The two fields stay factored so that resolvers, indexers, and roster checks can dispatch on `to` without parsing. The root the handle resolves under (org-scoped vs principal-scoped) is decided by the queue-dir resolver via the org-membership index, not by the handle string itself.

**Required on wire.** Post-collapse envelopes MUST emit both `to` and `handle`. There is no legacy synthesizer; envelopes missing `handle` fail to deserialize. The earlier `inbox:default` / namespaced-prefix vocabulary is gone.

from.description: DID of the sender (the principal whose scribe composed this envelope).

to.description: DID of the queue *owner* — the principal whose relay sequences this queue (per the owner-as-sequencer invariant). For self-owned channels this is the principal themselves; for org-scoped channels this is the org owner's DID (typically a `did:web` rooted on a domain the org controls). Together with `handle` forms the canonical wire address for the queue; the composite URI `<to>#<handle>` is display-only.

handle.description: Queue handle on the owner's machine — a bare slug, colon-pathed for tree nesting. Form: `<segment>(:<segment>)*` where each segment matches `[a-z_][a-z0-9_-]*`. Tree depth = colon depth (e.g. `dommage-corporel:paris-cohort`). No namespace prefix, no recognized vocabulary of top-level tokens — `assemblee_generale`, `triage`, `book-progress` are all valid bare-slug handles. See `tech.equanimi.secretariat.channelDef.handle` for the full grammar. Channel handles advertised by an org MUST appear in the org's `orgDoc.channels`. Required on wire.

depth.description: Declared attentional depth. Gross = surface-level, can be acknowledged peripherally. Subtle = needs deeper engagement.

urgency.description: Declared urgency. Inflationary by nature; the recipient's per-channel contract.local.md cadence governs whether it surfaces inline or queues for review.

source.description: Free-form origin of the work (e.g. Claude session ID, manual, agent name). Useful for retrospective traceability.

cadenceHint.description: Optional advisory hint to the receiver about when to surface (e.g. `morning`, `weekly`).

replyTo.description: Optional `DocHash` of a prior envelope's body that this envelope is replying to (form `sha256:<hex>`). Threads are chains of `replyTo` links; the root envelope of a thread omits this field. Wire-level only — thread materialization (collapsing a chain into an adapter's conversation view, e.g. Crisp session, Intercom thread) is the adapter's concern. Causality is cryptographic: the referenced hash must match a body the receiver actually has (or can request) for the link to verify, but the substrate does not enforce reachability — orphan replies are valid envelopes whose parent may arrive later or never.

title.description: Optional headline for the envelope, sender-declared. AG-shape: the *gross* surface of the body — what the recipient sees in a list/timeline before deciding to open. Author-populated in v0.3; AI-summarized variants may be auto-populated by the scribe in a later slice. Renderers SHOULD use this as the card title; absent, they fall back to the first heading in the body or the filename. Plain text; no markdown.

lede.description: Optional one-line summary, sender-declared. AG-shape: the *subtle* layer just beneath the title — what the recipient sees on hover/expand, before the full body. Author-populated in v0.3; AI-generated variants may follow. Renderers SHOULD use this as the preview line in dense timelines; absent, they fall back to slicing the first lines of the body. Plain text; no markdown.

summary.description: Optional multi-sentence abstract of the body, sender-declared. AG-shape: the *deepening pathway* — sender's own framing of what this envelope is about, useful when the body is long or technical. Author-populated in v0.3; AI-generated variants may follow. Renderers MAY display this in expanded card / detail views; not used in compact timeline rows. Plain text; markdown ignored in render.

agSource.description: Provenance marker for the `title`/`lede`/`summary` triplet. `human` (default, omitted on wire) — the author wrote them. `ai` — the scribe auto-populated them at envelope-write time because the author left them empty. Receivers MAY surface the distinction (badge, hover state) so AI-authored framing is never invisible. Per Secretariat's surface-don't-hide philosophy: the principal stamps; the AI drafts; the receiver decides what to do with that knowledge. Absent on legacy v0.3 envelopes whose AG fields were author-populated by definition — readers MUST treat absent as `human`.

delivered.description: Delivery state marker. `<relay-seq-id>` (opaque per-relay string) after the daemon federates the envelope and the relay confirms the write. `local` for envelopes addressed to self-owned channels under `~/.secretariat/channels/` that never federate. Absent (field omitted) means the envelope is undelivered — what earlier substrates expressed by placing the file under a `_drafts/` subtree. Substrate-for-themia Move 4 (2026-05-21) collapses the two filesystem locations into one (`<queue>/envelopes/YYYY/MM/DD/<rkey>.md`) with this field as the source of truth. Receiver-side: this field is informational; it travels on the wire so receivers can correlate cursors and detect drift, but trust still derives from `signature` (mandatory) and `$attestation` (selective).
